llm.summary: This bid-analysis skill is mostly coherent, but it handles device-linked registration, local credential storage, and login-bypass signed links in ways users should review carefully before installing.

dimensions.detail: Network access to the vendor API is expected for bid analysis, but sending platform, architecture, and a MAC-derived hash for account creation is privacy-sensitive and goes beyond simple report generation.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The manifest only declares ZLBX_API_KEY, while the artifact text describes fallback reads from ~/.zlbx/config.json, writes to ~/.zlbx/config.json, and HTML report generation under ~/zlbx-bid-decision-files/.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions disclose consent before registration and limit data collection, but they also require raw API-returned URLs with sk parameters to be displayed in chat and HTML output, which is an under-scoped handling rule for bearer-style access links.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill persists an API key outside the skill directory and generates shareable local HTML reports containing raw signed links; both are disclosed but carry meaningful credential and redistribution risk.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The bid-decision workflow and API querying fit the stated purpose, but the skill also directs automatic trial-account registration, device-feature collection, credential persistence, and preservation of signed login-bypass URLs in reports.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with the vendor API, consent-gated device fingerprinting for free-trial registration, API key storage in ~/.zlbx/config.json, and local HTML reports that may contain signed login-bypass links. Prefer configuring ZLBX_API_KEY yourself to skip auto-registration, and avoid forwarding generated reports unless signed links are removed or you accept that recipients may access those linked records.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: Local file reads for user-supplied bid files and local report writes are purpose-aligned and disclosed in the skill text, but not reflected in the minimal manifest metadata.
[TP4] expected: HTML report generation is a coherent report-export feature, not tool poisoning by itself; the concern is the default export plus sensitive link handling rather than the existence of branded output.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The auto-registration flow collects platform, architecture, and MAC hash, sends them to the vendor, and stores the returned API key locally. It is consent-gated and disclosed, but it expands the skill into device-linked account provisioning.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The registration and auto-login account lifecycle is only partly aligned with using the paid API; it is materially broader than bid analysis and should be reviewed as an account-management capability.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The report template and renderer preserve signed sk URLs and include them in visible output and local HTML, which can expose login-bypass links in shareable artifacts.
[SQP-2] expected: Local HTML creation is disclosed in the main skill and template, so it is not hidden, but default persistence of potentially sensitive business analysis still warrants user awareness.
[SSD-3] unexpected: The artifact explicitly treats sk as an免登录 signature and still requires it to be preserved in reports and citation links, making the scanner concern about token-like URL exposure supported.
[E1] unexpected: The external POST for auto-registration is artifact-backed and sends device-derived identifiers to the vendor; this is not malicious by itself because consent is required, but it is a material review concern.
